title: 4 ways to hire international remote workers | Ontop
summary: Contractor, EOR, freelance platform or your own entity: compare four ways to hire international remote workers by cost, control and compliance.
body_markdown:
There are four ways to hire international remote workers: engage them as independent contractors, employ them through an employer of record (EOR), hire them on a freelance platform, or set up your own legal entity in their country. Before cost or speed, answer one question: is this person a contractor or an employee? That answer decides which options are even open to you.


## The four options at a glance


Option Best fit Legal employer Speed to start Control


Independent contractor Project or ongoing work done with autonomy None (the contractor runs their own business) Fast Over deliverables, not hours or methods


Employer of record (EOR) Full-time employees in a country where you have no entity The EOR provider Moderate Day-to-day work, within local labor law


Freelance platform Short, well-defined tasks None Fast Limited to each gig


Your own foreign entity A large, long-term team in one country Your company Slow Full


## 1. Independent contractor agreements


Hiring an international remote worker as an independent contractor means you buy a service, not an employment relationship. The contractor invoices you, manages their own taxes in their country and decides how the work gets done.


### When contractors fit


Contractors fit when the work has a clear scope, the person sets their own schedule and methods, and they are free to work with other clients. That covers most engineering, design, marketing and operations roles that global teams fill first. Start from a solid[independent contractor agreement template](https://www.getontop.com/guides-reports/independent-contractor-agreement) .


### The risk to manage: misclassification


Classification depends on how the relationship works in practice, not on the title of the contract. Local tests differ by country, but most look at control over hours and methods, exclusivity, integration into your team and who carries the business risk. If those facts look like employment, authorities can reclassify the contractor as an employee and claim back taxes and benefits.


### Contractor of record: compliance without employment


A contractor of record engages contractors on your behalf, issues compliant agreements, carries the classification responsibility and pays them. Nobody becomes anyone's employer. This is the path Ontop is built for: contractor of record plus global contractor payroll in 150+ countries, starting from $49 per contractor per month ([Ontop pricing](https://www.getontop.com/pricing) , 2026). See how it works to[pay international contractors](https://www.getontop.com/solutions/pay-international-contractors) .


## 2. Employer of record (EOR) for full-time employees


An employer of record is a third party that becomes the legal employer of your worker in their country. It runs local payroll, withholds taxes, provides statutory benefits and issues an employment contract under local labor law, while you direct the day-to-day work.


### When an EOR fits


- The role is genuinely full-time employment, with fixed hours, exclusivity and integration into your team.
- The worker needs the statutory benefits and protections of a local employee.
- You have no legal entity in that country and do not want to open one yet.


### Costs and trade-offs


EOR providers charge a monthly fee per employee on top of salary, employer contributions and benefits. Because the worker is an employee, local rules on notice periods, severance and termination apply. You also depend on the provider's local setup for payroll accuracy and compliance.


### When you do not need one


If the people you hire are real contractors, an EOR adds employment costs to a relationship that does not require them. Ontop does not offer EOR. It is built for teams that can go global without one: read[when you don't need an EOR for contractors](https://www.getontop.com/solutions/eor-alternative-for-contractors) .


## 3. Freelance platforms


Freelance platforms are marketplaces where you post a task and hire from a pool of professionals. They work well for short, defined jobs. The trade-offs show up as you scale: fees on every contract, limited compliance coverage, contracts and payments spread across tools, and little continuity when you want to keep the same people long term.


## 4. Setting up a foreign entity


Opening a subsidiary or branch makes you a local employer with full control. It also brings company registration, local accounting, tax filings, payroll and labor counsel, and it usually takes months before the first hire. It makes sense when you plan a large, permanent team in a single country.


## How to choose the right option


### Start with classification


If the work is autonomous and project-based, you are choosing between a contractor setup and a freelance platform. If it is full-time employment, you are choosing between an EOR and your own entity.


### Then weigh cost, control and speed


- **Contractor of record:** the fastest compliant route for contractors, with predictable per-contractor pricing.
- **EOR:** employment without an entity, at a higher monthly cost per person.
- **Freelance platform:** quick for one-off tasks, harder to run as a long-term team.
- **Own entity:** maximum control, highest fixed cost and slowest start.


To compare what contractors cost in each market, use the[contractor cost by country calculator](https://www.getontop.com/calculator/contractor-cost-by-country) .


## Frequently asked questions


### Can I legally hire international remote workers as contractors?


Yes, as long as the relationship is a real contractor relationship under local rules: the worker controls how and when the work is done, can serve other clients and carries their own business risk.


### What is the difference between an EOR and a contractor of record?


An EOR becomes the legal employer of an employee. A contractor of record engages and pays independent contractors compliantly without creating employment.


### Do I need an EOR to hire remote workers abroad?


Only if you are hiring employees in a country where you have no entity. For contractors, a contractor of record covers agreements, compliance and payments.
